                        end
                    end

                    local kitBox = spawnObjectData(                                                             -- ... spawn the factionKitBox object...
                        {
                            data = table.remove(boxData, kitNum),                                                   -- ... using data from the boxData table, at the currently iterated index
                            position = Vector(posX + (5 * (factionNum-1)), posY, posZ - (8 * (playerNum - 1))),     -- ... spawn each factionKit at this calculated spot (moving successively with each spawn)
                            rotation = Vector(0, 180, 0)                                                            -- ... ensure each spawned object isn't rotated
                        }
                    )

                    break                                                                                   -- ... break the for loop early (the picked faction has been found)
                end
            end
        end

        Wait.frames(function()
            SmashUp.GameObjects.PlayerDecks[playerColor:lower().."Draw"] = factionDeck
            factionDeck.setName(playerColor.." Deck")                                                      -- ... set the name for the new deck
            factionDeck.setGMNotes(factionDeck.getName())                                                  -- ... set the GMNotes of the new deck
            factionDeck.setDescription("")                                                                 -- ... erase the description of the new deck
            factionDeck.setTags({"Deck", "Player", playerColor})
            factionDeck.shuffle()                                                                          -- ... shuffle the new deck
            factionDeck.deal(5, playerColor)                                                               -- ... draw 5 cards from the new deck
        end, 3)
    end
    dealTitans(deckRot)

    SmashUp.CustomExtras.spawnGeneralCustomExtras(spawnTheseCustomExtras, boxData)

    return boxData
end


-- this function creates the base deck from object data
local function createBaseDeck(boxData)
    local baseMat = SmashUp.GameObjects.BaseObjects.baseMat                                                             -- access the Base Mat object
    local baseDeckPos = baseMat.positionToWorld(baseMat.getSnapPoints()[1].position) + Vector(0, 0.5, 0)                -- get the spawn location on the mat where the base deck should be spawned
    local baseDeckRot = Vector(0, 180, 180)                                                                             -- set the default base deck rotation

    local basesKitData                                                                                                  -- setup this variable as local
    local promoBasesData                                                                                                -- setup this variable as local
    local deepReefCragData                                                                                              -- setup this variable as local
    local deepReefCragDeckID

    -- **find the Deepreef Crag card data and pull it out of the Big Box data, saving it in its own variable**
    for _, kitData in ipairs(boxData) do                                                                                -- for every factionKit in the Big Box...
        if kitData.Nickname == "Bases Kit" then                                                                         -- ... find the factionKit named "Bases Kit"...
            basesKitData = kitData                                                                                          -- ... and set this variable equal to Bases Kit data table
            for _, baseDeckData in ipairs(basesKitData.ContainedObjects) do                                                 -- ... for every deck of bases contained in the Bases Kit...
                if baseDeckData.Nickname == "Promos Bases" then                                                                 -- ... find the deck named "Promos Bases"...
                    promoBasesData = baseDeckData                                                                                   -- ... and set this variable equal to the Promos Bases deck data table
                    for baseCardNum, baseCardData in ipairs(promoBasesData.ContainedObjects) do                                     -- ... for every base card contained in the Promos Bases base deck...
                        if baseCardData.Nickname == "Deepreef Crag" then                                                                -- ... find the base card called "Deepreef Crag"...
                            deepReefCragData = table.remove(promoBasesData.ContainedObjects, baseCardNum)                                   -- ... and set this variable equal to Deepreef Crag's data table
                            deepReefCragDeckID = table.remove(promoBasesData.DeckIDs, baseCardNum)                                          -- ... and remove Deepreef Crag's DeckID entry from the Promos Base deck data
                            break
                        end
                    end
                    break                                                                                                           -- ... break early because we found the specified card
                end
            end
            break                                                                                                           -- ... break early because we found the specified deck of base cards
        end
    end

    -- **create the base deck that will be used in this match based on the settings selected by users**
    local baseDeck = nil                                                                                                -- establish this object variable as nil initially
    local needsCustomExpansionBases = false

    -- **this code creates a base deck using all bases from the utilized expansion sets**
    if SmashUp.XMLUI.xmlDataTables.toggleTracker["baseOptions"]["expansionBases"] then                                          -- if player's selected to include bases from the entire expansion...
        needsCustomExpansionBases = true

        for expansion in pairs(SmashUp.GameData.TableSetup.expansionsIncludedThisGame) do                                                              -- ... then for every expansion contained in the expansionBases table...
            for baseDeckNum = #basesKitData.ContainedObjects, 1, -1 do                                                              -- ... for every deck of bases in the Bases Kit data table...
                local baseDeckData = basesKitData.ContainedObjects[baseDeckNum]

                if baseDeckData.Nickname == expansion.." Bases" then                                                            -- ... if the iterated base deck's name equals that of the expansion's base deck
                    if expansion == "Promos" and SmashUp.XMLUI.xmlDataTables.toggleTracker["baseOptions"]["allPromoBases"] == false then    -- ... then if the iterated expansion is "Promos" AND player's selected to NOT include bases from all Promo factions (ie: treating all Promos as one expansion)...
                        for factionNum = #SmashUp.GameData.TableSetup.eachDraftedFactionsBaseCards, 1, -1 do                                                               -- ... iterating through each entry of the factionBases table, backwards (in order to see if any Promos factions WERE chosen, and therefore their bases need to be included)...
                            if SmashUp.GameData.TableSetup.eachDraftedFactionsBaseCards[factionNum].Description == "Promos" then                                               -- ... if the expansion of the iterated data for the faction's base deck is "Promos"...
                                baseDeck = createDeck(baseDeck, SmashUp.GameData.TableSetup.eachDraftedFactionsBaseCards[factionNum], baseDeckPos, baseDeckRot)                    -- ... then spawn/add the Promo faction's bases to the baseDeck
                            end
                        end
                    else                                                                                                            -- ... otherwise...
                        baseDeck = createDeck(baseDeck, table.remove(basesKitData.ContainedObjects, baseDeckNum), baseDeckPos, baseDeckRot) -- ... spawn/add the iterated data for the faction's bases to the baseDeck
                    end
                    break                                                                                                           -- ... break early because we found the base deck for the specified expansion
                end
            end
        end


    -- **this block creates a base deck using just the bases for the selected factions**
    elseif SmashUp.XMLUI.xmlDataTables.toggleTracker["baseOptions"]["factionBases"] then                                        -- otherwise, if player's selected to include only bases for played factions...
        for factionNum = #SmashUp.GameData.TableSetup.eachDraftedFactionsBaseCards, 1, -1 do                                                               -- ... iterating through the factionBases data table...
            baseDeck = createDeck(baseDeck, SmashUp.GameData.TableSetup.eachDraftedFactionsBaseCards[factionNum], baseDeckPos, baseDeckRot)                -- ... spawn/add the faction's bases to the base deck
        end

    -- **this block creates a base deck using ALL base cards in the game**
    -- **this block also creates a base deck using all REGULAR bases (no madness or monster bases)**
    elseif SmashUp.XMLUI.xmlDataTables.toggleTracker["baseOptions"]["allBases"] or SmashUp.XMLUI.xmlDataTables.toggleTracker["baseOptions"]["mostBases"] then
        needsCustomExpansionBases = true

        for baseDeckNum = #basesKitData.ContainedObjects, 1, -1 do
            local baseDeckData = basesKitData.ContainedObjects[baseDeckNum]
            if basesKitData.ContainedObjects[baseDeckNum].Nickname ~= "All Bases" then
                if (baseDeckData.Nickname == "Munchkin Bases" and (not SmashUp.GameData.TableSetup.nonStandardExpansionsIncluded["Munchkin"]))
                or (baseDeckData.Nickname == "Obligatory Cthulhu Bases" and (not SmashUp.GameData.TableSetup.nonStandardExpansionsIncluded["Cthulhu"])) then
                    goto bypass
                end
                baseDeck = createDeck(baseDeck, table.remove(basesKitData.ContainedObjects, baseDeckNum), baseDeckPos, baseDeckRot)
            end
            ::bypass::
        end
    end

    -- **this block adds bases for custom factions
    if next(SmashUp.GameData.Customs.draftedCustomFactions) ~= nil then
        for _, customFactionData in ipairs(SmashUp.GameData.Customs.allCustomFactionsAvailableToInstance_Array) do
            local factionName = customFactionData.factionName
            local creatorName = customFactionData.creator
            local factionLabel = factionName.." *&^* "..creatorName

            local customExpansion = customFactionData.expansion

            if SmashUp.GameData.Customs.draftedCustomFactions[factionLabel] then
                baseDeck = createDeck(baseDeck, customFactionData.baseData, baseDeckPos, baseDeckRot, true)

            elseif needsCustomExpansionBases and SmashUp.GameData.Customs.customExpansionsUsed[customExpansion] then
                baseDeck = createDeck(baseDeck, customFactionData.baseData, baseDeckPos, baseDeckRot, true)
                SmashUp.Database.factionTable[factionLabel] = {expansion = "Custom", customExpansion = customFactionData.expansion, description = customFactionData.description, compLevel = customFactionData.difficulty, included = false, custom = true, faction = factionName, creator = creatorName}
                SmashUp.GameData.Customs.databaseEntryBackup[factionLabel] = {expansion = "Custom", customExpansion = customFactionData.expansion, description = customFactionData.description, compLevel = customFactionData.difficulty, included = false, custom = true, faction = factionName, creator = creatorName}

            end
        end
    end

    -- **this block adds deepReefCrag promo base to the baseDeck
    if SmashUp.XMLUI.xmlDataTables.toggleTracker["baseOptions"]["promoBases"] then                              -- if player's selected to include the promo bases ("DeepreefCrag")...
        local deepReefCrag = spawnObjectData({                                                          -- ... then spawn the deepReefCrag base card from it's data...
            data = deepReefCragData,                                                                        -- ... using the base card data contained in this variable...
            position = {83.49, 2.21, 0},
            callback_function = function(spawnedObj)
                baseDeck.putObject(spawnedObj)
            end
        })
    else                                                                                                    -- otherwise (if player's have chosen not to include Deepreef Crag)...
        table.insert(promoBasesData.ContainedObjects, 1, deepReefCragData)                                  -- ... then put the card (via its data) back into the promoBases base deck...
        table.insert(promoBasesData.DeckIDs, 1, 6900)                                                       -- ... and put Deepreef Crag's DeckID back into the deck's data table
    end

    Wait.frames(function()                                                                                  -- wait 3 frames in order to...
        baseDeck.setName("Base Deck")                                                                           -- set the Base Deck's name
        baseDeck.setGMNotes(baseDeck.getName())                                                                 -- set the Base Deck's GMNote
        baseDeck.setDescription("")                                                                             -- erase the description field
        baseDeck.setTags({"Base", "Deck"})
        baseDeck.shuffle()                                                                                  -- ... shuffle the deck
    end, 3)
    SmashUp.GameObjects.BaseObjects.baseDraw = baseDeck
end


-- this function deals out base cards from the base deck to the base zones depending on how many players are in the game
local function dealBases()
    local baseCount                                                                                                                             -- establish this local variable which will represent the total number of bases that need to be dealt
    if SmashUp.XMLUI.xmlDataTables.toggleTracker["baseOptions"]["baseNumberOption1"] then baseCount = SmashUp.GameData.TurnControl.activePlayerCount               -- if player's selected to include one base per player, then baseCount equals the number of players
    elseif SmashUp.XMLUI.xmlDataTables.toggleTracker["baseOptions"]["baseNumberOption2"] then baseCount = SmashUp.GameData.TurnControl.activePlayerCount + 1       -- if player's selected to include one base per player plus one, then set the baseCount to the appropriate value
    end

    local baseDeck = SmashUp.GameObjects.BaseObjects.baseDraw                   -- ... obtain access to the baseDeck object
    for i = 1, baseCount do                                                         -- iterate through this code for as many bases as have been included in the game...
        local baseLoc = Global.getSnapPoints()[i].position                          -- ... identify the spawn position for the base cards using the base snap points on the board

        if i >= 7 then
            SmashUp.Bases.ExtraBaseDocks.addExtraBase(i)
        end

        local baseCard = baseDeck.takeObject(                                   -- ... take a base card from the baseDeck...
            {
                position = baseLoc,                                                     -- ... and put it at the appropriate spawn point
                flip = true,                                                            -- ... and flip the card face up
            }
        )

        baseCard.interactable = false
        SmashUp.Bases.BaseScoreboards.baseBlockStatus[i] = "dealing"            -- ... change status of this variable to "dealing" (not "on" or "off") in order to prevent dealing to the same base if the draw button is clicked while this card is being dealt

        SmashUp.makeSureMovementStops(baseCard)
        SmashUp.makeSureCardGetsUnlocked(baseCard)
    end
end

-- this function is called at the completion of the UI setup phase to setup the game board and deal out the cards
function DealCards.dealAll(contObjList)
    dealFactions(contObjList)                                                   -- call this function to deal out the faction decks to their respective players
    createBaseDeck(contObjList)                                                 -- call this function to create the base deck
    Wait.frames(function()                                                      -- after waiting 3 frames...
        dealBases()                                                             -- ... call this function to set out the base cards
    end, 3)

    return contObjList
end


function DealCards.onLoad(lib)
    SmashUp = lib
end

return DealCards

end)
__bundle_register("Smash Up/PlayZones", function(require, _LOADED, __bundle_register, __bundle_modules)
local Common = require("Common")

local SmashUp

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- THIS FILE CONTAINS THE FUNCTIONS NEEDED TO CREATE/SPAWN ALL THE ASSETS THAT ARE SPECIFIC TO EACH PALYERS' PLAYZONES (SUCH AS DISCLIGHTS, SCRIPTING ZONES, SNAP POINTS)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
local PlayZones = {
    DiscLights = require("Smash Up/DiscLights"),
}

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- THE FOLLOWING FUNCTIONS ARE USED TO PREPARE DATA/VARIABLES NECESSARY FOR CREATING EACH PLAYERS' PLAYZONE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- this function creates a table (playZoneColors) that holds the colors of each play zone, using the number of players in the game to properly distribute the colors on the top or bottom of the baseBlock
local function setPlayZoneColors()
    SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors = {bottomRow = {}, topRow = {}}                -- establish the playZoneColors table with a `bottomRow` and a `topRow`

    if SmashUp.GameData.TurnControl.activePlayerCount <= 2 then                                                -- if the number of players in this game is less than or equal to 2...
        local colorTable = {"Red", "Purple", "Blue", "Orange", "Yellow", "Green"}   -- ... create this table, used to determine color priority, and therefore which colors will appear first (on the `bottomRow`)
        local currentRow = "bottomRow"                                              -- ... start adding colors in the `bottomRow` section of the table
        for _, color in ipairs(colorTable) do                                       -- ... for each color in the colorTable...
            if SmashUp.GameData.UISetup.General.turnNumberByColor[color] then                                         -- ... if the color exists in the UISetup.General.turnNumberByColor table (meaning a player has chosen this color)...
                table.insert(SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors[currentRow], color)           -- ... then insert this color into the table
                currentRow = "topRow"                                                       -- ... and then move on to the `topRow`
            end
        end
        if #SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors.topRow < 1 then                        -- ... if no colors are added to the `topRow` (likely because there is only 1 player)...
            table.insert(SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors["topRow"], "White")           -- ... then add a "White" player to the `topRow`
        end

    elseif SmashUp.GameData.TurnControl.activePlayerCount == 3 then                                            -- if the number of players is 3...
        local colorTable = {"Red", "Green", "Purple", "Yellow", "Blue", "Orange"}   -- ... create this table, used to determine color priority, and therefore which colors will appear first (on the `bottomRow`)
        for _, color in ipairs(colorTable) do                                       -- ... for each color in the colorTable...
            if SmashUp.GameData.UISetup.General.turnNumberByColor[color] then                                         -- ... if the color exists in the UISetup.General.turnNumberByColor table (meaning a player has chosen this color)...
                table.insert(SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors["bottomRow"], color)          -- ... then add this color to both the `bottomRow`...
                table.insert(SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors["topRow"], color)             -- ... and the `topRow`
            end
        end

    elseif SmashUp.GameData.TurnControl.activePlayerCount == 4 then                                            -- if there are 4 players in this game...
        local colorTable = {"Red", "Purple", "Blue", "Orange", "Yellow", "Green"}   -- ... create this table, used to determine color priority, and therefore which colors will appear first (on the `bottomRow`)
        local currentRow = "bottomRow"                                              -- ... start in the `bottomRow`
        for i = 1, 6 do                                                             -- ... for each possible color (total of 6)...
            if SmashUp.GameData.UISetup.General.turnNumberByColor[colorTable[i]] then                                 -- ... if the color exists in the UISetup.General.turnNumberByColor table (meaning a player has chosen this color)...
                table.insert(SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors[currentRow], colorTable[i])   -- ... then add this color into the table
            end
            if #SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors[currentRow] == 2 then                  -- ... once there are 2 colors in the current row (`bottomRow`)...
                currentRow = "topRow"                                                       -- ... start adding colors to the `topRow`
                break                                                                       -- ... and break this for loop early
            end
        end
        if #SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors["bottomRow"] < 2 then                   -- ... if however, we got to this point, and only one color was added to the `bottomRow`...
            table.insert(SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors[currentRow], "White")         -- ... add a "White" player to the `bottomRow`...
            currentRow = "topRow"                                                       -- ... and switch to the `topRow`
        end

        for i = 6, 1, -1 do                                                         -- ... now, iterating backwards through the possible colors (total of 6)...
            if SmashUp.GameData.UISetup.General.turnNumberByColor[colorTable[i]] then                                 -- ... if the color exists in the UISetup.General.turnNumberByColor table (meaning a player has chosen this color)...
                table.insert(SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors[currentRow], colorTable[i])   -- ... then add this color into the table
            end
            if #SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors[currentRow] == 2 then                  -- ... once there are 2 colors in the current row (`topRow`)...
                break                                                                       -- ... break the for loop early
            end
        end
        if #SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors[currentRow] < 2 then                   -- ... once again, if we got to this point with only one color in the `topRow`...
            table.insert(SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors[currentRow], "White")         -- ... then add a "White" player to the `topRow`
        end

    elseif SmashUp.GameData.TurnControl.activePlayerCount >=5 then                                             -- if there are 5 or more players in this game...
        local colorTable = {"Red", "Purple", "Blue", "Green", "Yellow", "Orange"}   -- ... create this table, used to determine color priority, and therefore which colors will appear first (on the `bottomRow`)
        local currentRow = "bottomRow"                                              -- ... start in the `bottomRow`
        for i = 1, 6 do                                                             -- ... for each possible color (total of 6)...
            if i >= 4 then currentRow = "topRow" end                                    -- ... (once the iteration index is 4 or higher, switch to the `topRow`)
            if SmashUp.GameData.UISetup.General.turnNumberByColor[colorTable[i]] then                                 -- ... if the color exists in the UISetup.General.turnNumberByColor table (meaning a player has chosen this color)...
                table.insert(SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors[currentRow], colorTable[i])   -- ... add this color to the table
            else                                                                        -- ... otherwise, if the color is not found in the UISetup.General.turnNumberByColor table (meaning there is one color that hasn't been selected; ie, there are 5 players)...
                table.insert(SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors[currentRow], "White")         -- ... add a "White" player
            end
        end
    end
end



-- this function assigns starting positions and spacing intervals depending on how many players there are (more specifically, how many colors are on each side of the baseBlock)
local function determinePlayZoneElementSpacing()
    local playerZoneCount = #SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors.bottomRow                                 -- set this variable to the number of colors in one row of the playZoneColors table
    SmashUp.GameBoard.snapPoints = {}                                                                   -- establish `snapPoints` as an empty table

    if playerZoneCount == 1 then                                                                        -- if there is one color on each side of the baseBlock...
        SmashUp.GameBoard.centerOfFirstPlayerZone = SmashUp.GameBoard.zoneWidth / 2                     -- ... set the center of the first playerZone equal to half of the width of the baseBlock
        SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneSpacing = 0                                                           -- ... no space between play zones (there is, afterall, only 1 play zone on each side of the baseBlock)  (represents the distance between the start of one play zone, to the start of the next)
        SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneWidth = SmashUp.GameBoard.zoneWidth                                 -- ... sets the width of each players' play zone to the full width of a baseBlock

        SmashUp.GameBoard.snapPoints.snapPointCount = 9                                                 -- ... sets how many snap points there should be in one row
        SmashUp.GameBoard.zonePaddingX = 0.6
        SmashUp.GameBoard.zonePaddingZ = 0.6

    elseif playerZoneCount == 2 then                                                                    -- if there are 2 colors on each side of the baseBlock...
        SmashUp.GameBoard.centerOfFirstPlayerZone= SmashUp.GameBoard.halfWidth / 2                      -- ... set the center of the first playerZone equal to half the width of a "halfWidth" play zone (for 4 players)
        SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneSpacing = SmashUp.GameBoard.halfWidth + SmashUp.GameBoard.lineWidth   -- ... the distance from the start of one play zone to the start of the next
        SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneWidth = SmashUp.GameBoard.halfWidth                                 -- ... sets the width of each players' play zone to a halfWidth (half of the width of a baseBlock minus the width of a separation line)

        SmashUp.GameBoard.snapPoints.snapPointCount = 7                                                 -- ... sets how many snap points there should be in one row
        SmashUp.GameBoard.zonePaddingX = 0.4
        SmashUp.GameBoard.zonePaddingZ = 0.4

    elseif playerZoneCount == 3 then                                                                    -- if there are 3 colors on each side of the baseBlock...
        SmashUp.GameBoard.centerOfFirstPlayerZone = SmashUp.GameBoard.thirdWidth / 2                    -- ... set the center of the first playerZone equal to half the width of a "thirdWidth"
        SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneSpacing = SmashUp.GameBoard.thirdWidth + SmashUp.GameBoard.lineWidth  -- ... the distance from the start of one play zone to the start of the next
        SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneWidth = SmashUp.GameBoard.thirdWidth                                -- ... sets the width of each players' play zone to a thirdWidth (1/3 of the width of a baseBlock minus the width of both separation lines)

        SmashUp.GameBoard.snapPoints.snapPointCount = 5                                                 -- ... sets how many snap points there should be in one row
        SmashUp.GameBoard.zonePaddingX = 0.4
        SmashUp.GameBoard.zonePaddingZ = 0.4
    end
end




--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- THE FOLLOWING FUNCTIONS CREATE/SPAWN THE ELEMENTS IN EACH PLAYERS' PLAY ZONE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- this function is called after a snapPoint is added to the snapPoint table
-- this function calculates the position of the snapPoints opposite (where it would be if in the `topRow`), and adds that to the table
local function addOppositeSnap(snapTable, xPos, yPos, zPos, zoneCount, centralZ)
    if SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors.topRow[zoneCount] ~= "White" and SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors.topRow[zoneCount] ~= nil then

        zPos = centralZ + (centralZ - zPos)

        local newSnap = {
            position = Vector(xPos, yPos, zPos),
            rotation = Vector(0, 0, 0),
            rotation_snap = false,
            tags = {SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors.topRow[zoneCount]},
        }

        table.insert(snapTable, newSnap)
    end

    return snapTable
end



local function addSnapToTable(snapTable, xPos, yPos, zPos, zoneCount, centralZ)
    if SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors.bottomRow[zoneCount] ~= "White" and SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors.bottomRow[zoneCount] ~= nil then
        local newSnap = {
            position = Vector(xPos, yPos, zPos),
            rotation = Vector(0, 180, 0),
            rotation_snap = false,
            tags = {SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors.bottomRow[zoneCount]},
        }

        table.insert(snapTable, newSnap)
    end

    snapTable = addOppositeSnap(snapTable, xPos, yPos, zPos, zoneCount, centralZ)

    return snapTable
end


-- this function iterates and calculates the snap point positions
local function calculateSnaps(centralPosition, baseNum)
    local cardWidth = SmashUp.GameBoard.CARDWIDTH
    local cardHeight = SmashUp.GameBoard.CARDHEIGHT

    local xPosInit, yPosInit, zPosInit = centralPosition:get()
    yPosInit = 0.9611349

    local snapConvertX = 1
    local snapConvertZ = 1

    local snapTable

    if baseNum >= 7 then
        xPosInit = 0
        yPosInit = 0.5
        zPosInit = 0
        snapConvertX = SmashUp.GameBoard.zoneWidth / 10
        snapConvertZ = SmashUp.GameBoard.zoneHeight / 10

        snapTable = SmashUp.GameObjects.BaseObjects.extraBases[baseNum].getSnapPoints()
    else
        snapTable = Global.getSnapPoints()
    end

    local playZoneEdgeX = xPosInit - ((SmashUp.GameBoard.zoneWidth / 2) / snapConvertX)
    local playZoneEdgeZ = zPosInit - ((SmashUp.GameBoard.baseHeight / 2) / snapConvertZ)
    local startingPointX = playZoneEdgeX + ((SmashUp.GameBoard.zonePaddingX + (cardWidth / 2)) / snapConvertX)
    local startingPointZ = playZoneEdgeZ - ((SmashUp.GameBoard.zonePaddingZ + (cardHeight / 2)) / snapConvertZ)

    local xPos = startingPointX
    local yPos = yPosInit
    local zPos = startingPointZ

    local snapPointSpacing = (((SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneWidth - (SmashUp.GameBoard.zonePaddingX * 2) - cardWidth)) / (SmashUp.GameBoard.snapPoints.snapPointCount - 1)) / snapConvertX

    for zoneCount = 1, #SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors.bottomRow do
        for snapPointCount = 1, SmashUp.GameBoard.snapPoints.snapPointCount do
            for row = 0, 1 do
                for offset = 0, 1 do
                    if offset == 1 and snapPointCount == SmashUp.GameBoard.snapPoints.snapPointCount then break end
                    local xParam = xPos + (offset * (1.0125 / snapConvertX))
                    local zParam = (zPos - (row * (5.322 / snapConvertZ))) - (offset * (1.031 / snapConvertZ))

                    snapTable = addSnapToTable(snapTable, xParam, yPos, zParam, zoneCount, zPosInit)
                end
            end
            xPos = xPos + snapPointSpacing
        end
        xPos = startingPointX + ((SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneSpacing / snapConvertX) * zoneCount)
    end

    if baseNum >= 7 then
        SmashUp.GameObjects.BaseObjects.extraBases[baseNum].setSnapPoints(snapTable)
    else
        Global.setSnapPoints(snapTable)                                                                                 -- set the Global snapPoints with the new data
    end
end


-- this function creates the ScriptZones surrounding each players' playZone
local function spawnScriptZone(xPos, yPos, zPos, color, baseBlockNum)
    local zone = spawnObject(                                                               -- spawn an object (and call it a `zone` object)
        {
            type="ScriptingTrigger",                                                        -- ... object is a ScriptingTrigger (script zone)
            position = Vector(0, 1000, 0),                                                  -- ... spawn it at these coordinates (way up high to avoid the flashing appearance as it spawns)
            scale = {SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneWidth, 1.35, SmashUp.GameBoard.boxHeight},   -- ... increase the size in the x- and z-axes to fill the player's playZone
            sound = false                                                                   -- ... spawning the object should not make a sound
        }
    )
    Wait.frames(function()
        zone.setPosition(Vector(xPos, yPos, zPos))
    end, 1)

    zone.setName(color.."Zone"..baseBlockNum)                                               -- give the script zone a name
    zone.setGMNotes(zone.getName())                                                         -- assign the GMNotes the same value as the name
    zone.setTags({"Action", "Minion", "Titan", "Token", color})                             -- add tags to the script zone
    zone.interactable = false                                                               -- make sure the object can't be interacted with by players (clicking etc)
    zone.locked = true                                                                      -- make the zone locked

    SmashUp.GameObjects.ScriptingZones.playerColorPlayZones[baseBlockNum] = SmashUp.GameObjects.ScriptingZones.playerColorPlayZones[baseBlockNum] or {}     -- establish this sub-table in the GameObjects objectTable
    SmashUp.GameObjects.ScriptingZones.playerColorPlayZones[baseBlockNum][color] = zone                                                                 -- add this scripting zone object to the objectTable
end


-- this function performs the actual spawning of the DiscLight
local function spawnGlowDisc(xPos, yPos, zPos, discRot, color, baseBlockNum)

    local discURL = {                               -- establish this table to obtain the URL of the DiscLight assetBundle depending on which color needs to be spawned
        Red = [[https://steamusercontent-a.akamaihd.net/ugc/1787359981062565674/4B441820067F6DF607C1F7BACC4A36ECA197EA3F/]],

-- this function receives the numerical identifier for the baseBlock, as well as it's center position, and starts the process of spawning each of the play zone elements
function PlayZones.spawnPlayZoneElements(baseBlockNum, positionVector)
    local currentRow = "bottomRow"                                                          -- start the process in the `bottomRow`
    local discRot = 0                                                                       -- the DiscLights should not be rotated in the `bottomRow`
    local xPosInit, yPosInit, zPosInit = positionVector:get()                               -- identify these 3 variables from the vector passed into this function
    local xPos = (xPosInit - (SmashUp.GameBoard.zoneWidth / 2)) + SmashUp.GameBoard.centerOfFirstPlayerZone        -- calculate the x-axis spawning location for the DiscLight and the ScriptZone
    local yPos = yPosInit --+ 0.05                                                            -- calculate the y-axis spawning location
    local zPos = zPosInit - 16.88701                                                        -- calculate the z-axis spawning location for the DiscLights
    local zPosScptZn = zPosInit - 11.49009                                                  -- calculate the z-axis spawning location for the ScriptZones

    calculateSnaps(positionVector, baseBlockNum)                                            -- ... call this function to generate the snapPoints for each players' play zone

    for y = 1, 2 do                                                                         -- for each row in a baseBlock (`bottomRow` and `topRow`)...
        local reset_xPos = xPos                                                             -- ... set this variable to reset the xPos variable back to its starting value

        for x = 1, #SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors["bottomRow"] do                        -- ... for each color (player) in the current row...
            local color = SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors[currentRow][x]                       -- ... identify the color for this play zone from the playZoneColors table
            if color ~= "White" and color ~= nil then                                           -- ... as long as the color isn't "White" or nil...
                spawnGlowDisc(xPos, yPos, zPos, discRot, color, baseBlockNum)                       -- ... call the spawnGlodDisc function to spawn the appropriate DiscLights
                spawnScriptZone(xPos, yPos, zPosScptZn, color, baseBlockNum)                        -- ... call this function to create a scripting zone for each players' play zone
            end
            xPos = xPos + SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneSpacing                                     -- ... increment the xPosition by the playZoneSpacing value
        end

        xPos = reset_xPos                                                                   -- ... reset xPos back to its starting value

        currentRow = "topRow"                                                               -- ... switch row to the `topRow`
        zPos = zPosInit + 16.88701                                                          -- ... re-calculate the starting location of z-axis (will now be above the base card)
        zPosScptZn = zPosInit + 11.49009                                                    -- ... re-calculate the starting x-axis location of the player's play zone scripting zone
        discRot = 180                                                                       -- ... the DiscLights should not be rotated 180 deg
    end
end

-- this function obtains the Vector positions of the center of each main baseBlock on the GameBoard, and stores them in the table
local function createBaseBlockZonePositionsTable()
    local xInc = 38.01448171                                                    -- establish these local variables to be used in setting up a table (follows next in the code)
    local xPos = -38.01448171
    local yPos = 0.76                                                           -- this is the level of the top surface of the board (board's y-center is at -1.25; board's thickness is 4.0)
    local zPos = -19.0929878

    SmashUp.GameBoard.BaseBlockZonePositions = {}                                    -- establish this empty table variable
    for i = 1, 2 do                                                             -- for each major row of base blocks (total of 2)...
        for j = 1, 3 do                                                         -- ... and for each base block in each row (total of 3)...
            local vect = Vector(xPos, yPos, zPos)                                   -- ... set this vector variable consisting of the establixhed x, y, and z components
            table.insert(SmashUp.GameBoard.BaseBlockZonePositions, vect)            -- ... insert this vector into the BaseBlockZonePositions table
            xPos = xPos + xInc                                                      -- ... increment the x position by the required amount (xInc)
        end
        xPos = -xInc                                                            -- ... reset xPos to its starting position (which just so happens to be the negative of xInc)
        zPos = -zPos                                                            -- ... set zPos to its negative value
    end
end


-- this function iterates through each baseBlock region and spawns a DiscLight and a ScriptZone for each player, and sets the snap points as well
local function addPlayZoneElements()
    createBaseBlockZonePositionsTable()                                         -- this function is called to obtain the Vector positions of the center of each main baseBlock, and store them in a table

    for baseBlockNum = 1, 6 do                                                  -- for each main baseBlock on the GameBoard (1 through 6)...
        PlayZones.spawnPlayZoneElements(baseBlockNum, SmashUp.GameBoard.BaseBlockZonePositions[baseBlockNum])   -- ... call this function on the iterated baseBlock, using its center position Vector as the starting point for spawning the elements
    end
end



-- this function sets the class of the various object XML elements in order to activate the lines, and provide them with the appropriate players' colors
local function activateLines()
    local numPlayer = #SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors.bottomRow * 2           -- the number of players will be equal to the number of colors contained in this table's bottomRow times 2

    for row, colorList in pairs(SmashUp.GameBoard.playZoneColors) do            -- for each row sub-table in the playZoneColors table...
        local side                                                              -- ... establish this local variable
        if row == "bottomRow" then                                              -- ... if row is "bottomRow", then side equals "down"
            side = "down"
        elseif row == "topRow" then                                             -- ... if row is "topRow", then side equals "up"
            side = "up"
        end

        for slot, color in ipairs(colorList) do                                 -- ... for each entry in the currently iterated rows list of player colors...
            for i = 1, 6 do                                                         -- ... then for each (total of 6) individual baseBlocks...
                SmashUp.GameObjects.board.UI.setClass(numPlayer.."p_z"..i.."_"..side..slot, numPlayer.."player "..color)    -- ... using the numPlayer, side, slot (index of the color in this table), and the color at this index in the table, identify the appropriate XML element, and assign it a color via its class
            end

            for i = 7, 14 do                                                        -- ...and for each extraBaseDock (total of 8)...
                SmashUp.GameObjects.BaseObjects.extraBases[i].UI.setClass(numPlayer.."p_"..side..slot, numPlayer.."player "..color)    -- ... using the numPlayer, side, slot (index of the color in this table), and the color at this index in the table, identify the appropriate XML element, and assign it a color via its class
            end
        end
    end
    SmashUp.GameObjects.board.UI.setClass("boardXML", "fullFrame "..numPlayer.."playerSetup")   -- assign the parent xml element (boardXML) a class that includes the number of players, which in turn will activate the appropriate children
end


-- this function uses the playZoneColors table, and the calculated measurements to start spawning the elements for each players' play zones
local function setupPlayerZones()

    activateLines()                     -- this function activates the XML lines in each base block, and assigns them the appropriate colors
    addPlayZoneElements()               -- this function ultimately creates/spawns all of the baseBlock elements for each player
end



-- this function is called from the GameSetup file (GameBoard.boardSetup) to setup each players' playzone on the main 6 baseBlocks
function PlayZones.createPlayZones()
    -- SmashUp = lib

    setPlayZoneColors()                                                         -- call this function to create the table (playZoneColors) that is used to indicate the colors of each play zone
    determinePlayZoneElementSpacing()                                           -- call this function to calculate the needed spacing intervals to properly place playzone-specific elements
    setupPlayerZones()                                                          -- call this function to place/spawn playzone-specific elements
end


function PlayZones.onLoad(lib)
    SmashUp = lib

    PlayZones.DiscLights.onLoad(SmashUp)
end

-- this function is run when the game loads, to generate the UI panels to select expansions and factions
local function buildExpansionFactionXMLData(xmlTable, Database)
    local UIExpansionTable = {}
    local UIFactionTable = {}                                   -- create a table that will ultimately be added to the getXmlTable for generating the UI

    local expansionList = Database.expansionList
    local expansionCount = 0

    for i = 1, #expansionList do                                                -- for every expansion in the expansionList...
        local expansion = expansionList[i]
        if expansion ~= "Decks" then                                            -- ... as long as the expansion is not a generic `Decks` expansion...
            expansionCount = expansionCount + 1

            -- BUILD EXPANSION TOGGLES FOR THE `SELECT EXPANSIONS` PANEL
            local expansionToggle = {
                tag = "Toggle",
                attributes = {
                    id = expansion,
                    text = expansion,
                }
            }
            -- table.insert(UIExpansionTable, expansionToggle)
            UIExpansionTable[expansionCount] = expansionToggle


            -- BUILD EXPANSION TOGGLES FOR THE 'SELECT FACTIONS' PANEL (and setup the GridLayout that will hold the factions)
            local expansionSetSection = {                   -- establish a table variable called expansionSetSection that will be added to UITable. every table generated here becomes an expansion section in the UI
                tag = "VerticalLayout",                     -- This is the "parent" UI element for an expansion...
                children = {                                -- ... and it's children are placed starting here
                    {
                        tag = "Toggle",                     -- The first child is a toggle for the expansion set
                        attributes = {
                            id = "set-"..expansion,
                            text = expansion,
                        }
                    },
                    {
                        tag = "GridLayout",                 -- the second child is a GridLayout that will hold all the individual faction toggles
                        attributes = {
                            class = "factionGrid"
                        },
                        children = {}                       -- setup a table here within the GridLayout that will hold all the faction toggle elements as children of the GridLayout
                    }
                }
            }                                               -- the first portion of the UI expansion set table ends here

            -- BUILD THE FACTION TOGGLES FOR THE `SELECT FACTIONS' PANEL
            local factionList = Database.factionsByExpansion[expansion]     -- obtain a list of factions for the current iterated expansion from factionsByExpansion table
            local factionGridChildren = expansionSetSection.children[2].children
            -- for factionNo, faction in ipairs(factionList) do                -- for each faction in the list of factions...
            for factionNo = 1, #factionList do
                local faction = factionList[factionNo]
                local factionTable = {                                      -- ... create a table that holds the UI element info for an individual faction...
                    tag = "Toggle",
                    attributes = {
                        id = faction,
                        text = faction,
                    }
                }
                -- table.insert(factionGridChildren, factionTable)        -- ... and inserts that factionTable into the GridLayout's children table, which itself is a part of the expansion set's vLayout table
                factionGridChildren[factionNo] = factionTable
            end
            -- table.insert(UIFactionTable, expansionSetSection)               -- insert the completed expansion table into the overall UITable
            UIFactionTable[expansionCount] = expansionSetSection

            SmashUp.GameData.UISetup.General.factionScrollWindowHeight = SmashUp.GameData.UISetup.General.factionScrollWindowHeight + 1                       -- 1 for each expansion toggle
            SmashUp.GameData.UISetup.General.factionScrollWindowHeight = SmashUp.GameData.UISetup.General.factionScrollWindowHeight + math.ceil(#factionList / 2)
        end
    end

    -- table.insert(UIExpansionTable, {tag = "Toggle", attributes = {id = "Custom", text = "Custom", active = "false"}})
    expansionCount = expansionCount + 1
    UIExpansionTable[expansionCount] = {tag = "Toggle", attributes = {id = "Custom", text = "Custom", active = "false"}}

    local customSpots = {
        tag = "VerticalLayout",
        children = {
            {
                tag = "Toggle",
                attributes = {
                    id = "set-Custom",
                    text = "Custom",
                    active = "false",
                }
            },
            {
                tag = "GridLayout",
                attributes = {
                    class = "factionGrid",
                },
                children = {}
            }
        }
    }

    local customChildren = customSpots.children[2].children
    for customNo = 1, SmashUp.GameData.Customs.maximumCustomQuant, 1 do
        -- table.insert(customChildren, {tag = "Toggle", attributes = {id = "customToggle"..customNo, text = "customToggle"..customNo, active = "false"}})
        customChildren[customNo] = {tag = "Toggle", attributes = {id = "customToggle"..customNo, text = "customToggle"..customNo, active = "false"}}
    end
    table.insert(UIFactionTable, customSpots)

    local rootPanel = xmlTable[4]
    local expansionPanel = rootPanel.children[1].children[1].children[5]

    local factionPanel = rootPanel.children[2].children[1].children[5].children[1]
    local factionPanelAttributes = factionPanel.attributes

    expansionPanel.children = UIExpansionTable                                   -- ... then place the UIExpansionTable into its correct location...
    factionPanel.children = UIFactionTable                                       -- ... and put the UIFactionTable into the correct location of the UI XML table...
    factionPanelAttributes.height = (SmashUp.GameData.UISetup.General.factionScrollWindowHeight * 20) + 5

    return xmlTable
end

-- this function is run when the game is loaded in order to construct the Open Draft panel xml from code
local function buildFreePickXMLData(xmlTable, Database)

    local accommodateForCustoms = 10
    local maxRows = 0 + accommodateForCustoms

    for loopNum = 1, 2 do
        local portionToEdit
        local labelAppend

        local draftRoot = xmlTable[5]
        local rightPanel = draftRoot.children[2].children[2]

        if loopNum == 1 then
            local scrollContainer = rightPanel.children[3].children[1]
            portionToEdit = scrollContainer.children
            labelAppend = ""

        elseif loopNum == 2 then
            local scrollContainer = rightPanel.children[4].children[1].children[1]
            portionToEdit = scrollContainer.children
            labelAppend = "_scroll"

        end

        for expansion, factionList in pairs(Database.factionsByExpansion) do
            if expansion ~= "Decks" then
                maxRows = maxRows + math.ceil(#factionList / 4)
            end
        end

        local portionCount = 0

        for i = 1, maxRows do                                   -- for rows 1 through 23 of the right-sided draft panel of the UI (these rows are added to make sure there is enough room to hold ALL factions, in addition to the 9 rows that are already hard-coded in the xml file)...
            elementCount = 0

            local newRow = {                                    -- ... create a new table that represents a VerticalLayout element (this vlayout will hold a panel (to display expansion name text) and a HorizontalLayout (that will show 4 faction boxes))...
                tag = "VerticalLayout",
                children = {}
            }

            local panelTextPortion = {                              -- ... create the Panel element table...
                tag = "Panel",
                attributes = {
                    id = "draftRow"..i.."_label"..labelAppend,                                   -- ... label it appropriately...
                    class = "draftRowLabel"
                },
                children = {
                    {                                               -- ... add the child text element...
                        tag = "Text",
                        attributes = {
                            id = "draftRow"..i.."_labelText"..labelAppend
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            -- table.insert(newRow.children, panelTextPortion)     -- ... and add the panel element to the parent VerticalLayout element...
            elementCount = elementCount + 1
            newRow.children[elementCount] = panelTextPortion


            local draftRowPortion = {                           -- ... then, create the HorizontalLayout (faction/draft row) element...
                tag = "HorizontalLayout",
                attributes = { id = "draftRow"..i..labelAppend },
                children = {}
            }

            for j = 1, 4 do                                                 -- ... and for every draftable faction in this row (1 to 4)...
                local draftBoxNum = (((i - 1) * 4) + j)
                local draftBoxID = "draftBox"..draftBoxNum..labelAppend         -- ... generate the id name of the draftBox based on what row and cell is being iterated...
                local draftBox = {                                              -- ... and create the draftBox VerticalLayout element...
                    tag = "VerticalLayout",
                    attributes = {
                        id = draftBoxID                                         -- ... label it appropriately...
                    },
                    children = {                                                -- ... and add all of the draftBox children including...
                        [1] = {
                            tag = "Image",                                      -- ... the image of the faction...
                            attributes = { id = "image_"..draftBoxID}
                        },
                        [2] = {
                            tag = "Text",                                       -- ... the name of the faction...
                            attributes = { id = "text_"..draftBoxID}
                        },
                        [3] = {
                            tag = "Button",                                     -- ... and the button to complete the drafting...
                            attributes = { id = "button_"..draftBoxID}
                        }
                    }
                }
                -- table.insert(draftRowPortion.children, draftBox)    -- ... then add each draftBox VerticalLayout element to the HorizontalLayout row element...
                draftRowPortion.children[j] = draftBox
            end
            -- table.insert(newRow.children, draftRowPortion)      -- ... and then add the HorizontalLayout row element to the parent VerticalLayout element
            elementCount = elementCount + 1
            newRow.children[elementCount] = draftRowPortion

            portionCount = portionCount + 1
            portionToEdit[portionCount] = newRow
            -- table.insert(portionToEdit, newRow)                 -- finally, add each newly generated row to the xmlTable (via portionToEdit subTable)
        end
    end

    return xmlTable
end


local function addRowsToCustomTable(xmlTable)
    local xmlChildren = {}

    for rowNum = 0, SmashUp.GameData.Customs.maximumCustomQuant do
        local rowID = "customRow"..rowNum
        local newRow = {tag = "HorizontalLayout", attributes = {id = rowID, class = "customRowPicker", active = "false"}, children = {}}

        local typeTable

        if rowNum == 0 then
            typeTable = {{type = "Faction", size = 585}}
        else
            -- typeTable = {{type = "Faction", size = 137.31818}, {type = "Expansion", size = 140.77273}, {type = "Creator", size = 123.5}, {type = "Date", size = 101.90909}, {type = "Extra", size = 59.59091}}
            typeTable = {{type = "Faction", size = 140}, {type = "Expansion", size = 160}, {type = "Creator", size = 125}, {type = "Date", size = 100}, {type = "Extra", size = 60}}
        end

        -- for index, cellInfo in ipairs(typeTable) do
        for index = 1, #typeTable do
            local cellInfo = typeTable[index]
            local rowCellType = rowID.."_"..cellInfo.type

            newRow.children[index] = {tag = "Panel", attributes = {id = rowCellType, class = "customFactionRow", minWidth = cellInfo.size, preferredWidth = cellInfo.size}}
            if rowNum == 0 then
                newRow.children[index].children = {tag = "Text", attributes = {id = rowCellType.."_Text", text = "Populating list of custom factions from database...", alignment = "MiddleCenter", fontStyle = "Bold", fontSize = "17", verticalOverflow = "Overflow", active = "true"}}
            else
                if cellInfo.type == "Extra" then
                    newRow.children[index].children = {tag = "Image", attributes = {id = rowCellType.."_Image", class="customFactionRowExtraImage"}}
                else
                    newRow.children[index].children = {tag = "Text", attributes = {id = rowCellType.."_Text", class="customFactionRowText"}}
                end
            end


            if cellInfo.type == "Faction" then
                newRow.children[index].attributes.childAlignment = "MiddleLeft"
            end
        end

        xmlChildren[rowNum + 1] = newRow
        -- table.insert(xmlChildren, newRow)
    end

    xmlTable[6].children[1].children[3].children[2].children[1].children = xmlChildren

    return xmlTable
end

-- this is the function that is called at load-up, which then calls individual functions that build individual xml portions
local function addXmlViaCode(Database)
    local xmlTable = UI.getXmlTable()           -- access the UIs XML table...

    xmlTable = buildExpansionFactionXMLData(xmlTable, Database)
    xmlTable = buildFreePickXMLData(xmlTable, Database)

    xmlTable = addRowsToCustomTable(xmlTable)

    UI.setXmlTable(xmlTable)                    -- ... and then set the new table as the completed UI XML
end

This is useful to detect changes to a player, in particular, player color for using the `xmlFunctions.changeSetUpUIVisibility` function

-- FUNCTION THAT INITIALIZES ALL REQUIRED UI ELEMENTS WHEN THE GAME IS LOADED. APPEARS AT THE BOTTOM SO THAT ALL LOCAL FUNCTIONS ARE CREATED FIRST.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function XMLUI.xmlSetup.registerXMLFunctions()
    for page, funcSet in pairs(XMLUI) do
        if page == "xmlUserInput" then
            for funcName, func in pairs(funcSet) do
                if funcName ~= "onLoad" then
                    local varName = string.format("%s.%s", page, funcName)
                    _G[varName] = func
                end
            end
        elseif page == "SettingsPanel" then
            for funcName, func in pairs(funcSet) do
                if funcName ~= "calculateAvailableFactionsPerPlayer" and funcName ~= "onLoad" then
                    local varName = string.format("%s.%s", page, funcName)
                    _G[varName] = func
                end
            end
        elseif page == "RandomSelectionPanel" then
            for funcName, func in pairs(funcSet) do
                if funcName:find("^faction") or funcName:find("Clicked") then
                    local varName = string.format("%s.%s", page, funcName)
                    _G[varName] = func
                end
            end
        elseif page == "DraftSelectionPanel" then
            for funcName, func in pairs(funcSet) do
                if funcName:find("^draft") or funcName:find("Clicked") then
                    local varName = string.format("%s.%s", page, funcName)
                    _G[varName] = func
                end
            end
        elseif page == "OptionsPanel" then
            for funcName, func in pairs(funcSet) do
                if funcName:find("^update") and funcName:find("Input$") then
                    local varName = string.format("%s.%s", page, funcName)
                    _G[varName] = func
                end
            end
        elseif page == "FirstPlayerTurnSettings" then
            for funcName, func in pairs(funcSet) do
                if funcName == "clickColorBoxToggle" then
                    local varName = string.format("%s.%s", page, funcName)
                    _G[varName] = func
                end
            end
        elseif page == "CustomDecks" then
            for funcName, func in pairs(funcSet) do
                if funcName ~= "onLoad" then
                    local varName = string.format("%s.%s", page, funcName)
                    _G[varName] = func
                end
            end
        elseif page == "BugReports" then
            for funcName, func in pairs(funcSet) do
                if funcName ~= "onLoad" then
                    local varName = string.format("%s.%s", page, funcName)
                    _G[varName] = func
                end
            end
        elseif page == "BeginPanel" then
            for funcName, func in pairs(funcSet) do
                if funcName:find("startUI") then
                    local varName = string.format("%s.%s", page, funcName)
                    _G[varName] = func
                end
            end
        end
    end
end



function XMLUI.xmlSetup.onLoad(lib)
    SmashUp = lib

    XMLUI.xmlSetup.registerXMLFunctions()

    establishPlayersWithValidColorsTable()

    addXmlViaCode(SmashUp.Database)                                                 -- this function generates the Expansion/Faction selection UI

    setupXMLUIToggleTable(SmashUp.Database)                                            -- this function is called to establish a table (toggleTracker) that will track the on/off status of each toggle used throughout the UI

    XMLUI.xmlUserInput.onLoad(SmashUp)

local function setRedrawSettingsTable()

-- this function is called during various processes that end up changing the appearance of the redraw options panel.
-- this function will make interactable, or uninteractable, the redraw options panel elements based on the status of the `redraws allowed?` toggle

-- this function is run whenever the redraw options panel `cancel` button is clicked
function OptionsPanel.redrawCancel()

    UI.setAttribute("redrawAllow", "isOn", XMLUI.xmlDataTables.redrawSettings.redrawsActivated)                                -- explicitly update the `redraw allow` toggle's `isOn` attribute according to the saved status

    if XMLUI.xmlDataTables.redrawSettings.toggleOption == 1 then                                                        -- if the first option in the toggle group is selected...
        XMLUI.xmlDataTables.toggleTracker["optionToggles"]["redrawOption1"] = true                                      -- ... update the toggleTracker table accordingly (first toggle is true, second toggle is false)..
        XMLUI.xmlDataTables.toggleTracker["optionToggles"]["redrawOption2"] = false

-- this function is called when the inputField or slider of the redraw options panel are changed
function OptionsPanel.updateRedrawInput(playerInst, countVal, inputID)
    UI.setAttribute("redrawInput", "text", countVal)                       -- set the inputField text attribute to the new value
    UI.setAttribute("redrawSlider", "value", countVal)                     -- set the slider value attribute to the new value
end


function OptionsPanel.resetRedraw(playerID)
    setRedrawSettingsTable()
    OptionsPanel.redrawCancel()

    UI.setAttribute(playerID.."_redraw","interactable", "true")             -- ... make sure the redraw button will be interactable...
    UI.setAttribute(playerID.."_redrawButtonWindow", "active", "false")     -- ... even though the redraw button's parent panel will be hidden/inactive

    UI.setAttribute(playerID.."_redraw_scroll","interactable", "true")             -- ... make sure the redraw button will be interactable...
    UI.setAttribute(playerID.."_redrawButtonWindow_scroll", "active", "false")     -- ... even though the redraw button's parent panel will be hidden/inactive
end
